summary.verdict: STRUCTURE adds a genuine ORTHOGONAL signal where SEQUENCE fails (a MODEST, honestly-bounded improvement — NOT a decisive ceiling-break): on all 4 phylogenetically-isolated pathogens, structural homology (Foldseek TM) discriminates targets better than sequence (pooled AUROC structure-TM 0.6903 vs sequence 0.6403, a modest +0.05, consistent 4/4), and of the 65 targets SEQUENCE could not see at all (no mmseqs homolog — the TID3 silent-failure cases), STRUCTURE recovers 29 (0.446) via a same-fold (TM>=0.5) reference-target homolog. So structure is a REAL orthogonal signal for the isolated-pathogen case that broke sequence-based target-ID — a partial rescue, not a solution. **KEY HONEST LIMIT (falsify-first on our own positive): the STRUCTURAL-CONSERVATION NULL is NOT yet run — i.e. whether structural-homology-to-TARGETS beats structural-homology-to-ANY-protein (the exact critique TID1 raised for sequence conservation). Some of the signal may be 'targets have target-like generic folds' rather than specific homology; the AUROC (target-vs-nontarget) partially controls this but does not decompose it. So: a modest, reproduced, orthogonal signal — the specificity is not yet established.** Further caveats: Foldseek E-values under-estimated (led with TM-score); AlphaFold predicted structures; hypotheses, not validated targets; not wet-lab.
